english: Father, I am going toward the herds with the young men. -- Do not go. You are young. -- When you were young, you were still in the villages(?). -- Of the village, two of my brothers did not come back; mother wept for us a year. -- But I want fame. -- Fame does not feed a man. Stay with your mother and plough my field. -- I will stay this year.

Son of the gods, your feet are heavy. -- When I was young I was faster than you. -- Who saw that? -- The horses saw it, and I beat them. -- Then where are those horses now? -- They have gone, and I am alive. -- Let us run to the river. -- I do not run.

Does your knee hurt? -- I do not hurt, I am tired. -- Come here and hear my words. Carry the ashes and honour the gods. -- I carry it. -- Do you watch me during the days? -- I watch you by day with the stars. -- May Dyeus protect you.

english: Good-minded one, my brother is hot(?) and does not eat. -- How many days does he lie? -- He lies three days. -- Bring me new water and a cup. -- I cook these roots and he drinks. -- Now he sweats, and the fever leaves your brother. -- Which roots do you know? -- My mother knew them and I learned hers from her.

To the old man: a boar has pierced my leg. -- Show me your leg. Do not tremble. Bring me leaves of the tree. -- Which leaves help? -- My mother showed them to me long ago. I bind your leg with a leaf. -- What shall I pay you? -- Kill the boar and give me its meat.

english: Orphan, I owe our house a cow. -- What do you owe us? -- He (gave?) us the gift of the lord in winter. When I left I paid my debt. I pay it this day, and now your debt goes away. -- Give us the best cow. -- What best one have I given? -- Now our name will be good.
